1. Add Inkcast to an MCP client

Step 1 — REST — GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp (rest, 2026-10-28T17:08:11Z)

The client asks the MCP endpoint who protects it: Inkcast's own authorization server.

✓ HTTP 200; the resource names its authorization server

Step 2 — REST — GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server (rest, 2026-10-28T17:08:11Z)

Discovery: where to register, authorize and get tokens; PKCE S256 is required.

✓ HTTP 200; metadata lists registration, authorization and token endpoints with S256

Step 3 — dynamic client registration (mcp, 2026-10-28T17:08:11Z)

The client registered itself (RFC 7591); no secret, PKCE instead.

✓ registered as “Walkthrough MCP client” (client_id aeb9cb4f-1d60-4a9c-8f7e-73608eef3ed6), redirect http://localhost:39527/callback
